translations.text: Since many have set their hand to write down an account, with full assurance, of the things that have been accomplished among us,
just as those who were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word from the beginning handed them down to us,
it seemed good to me also, having followed all things accurately from the first, to write them for you in order, O excellent lover of God,
so that you may know the certainty of the words in which you were instructed.

In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was . . . [?] whose name was Zechariah, of the daily course of the service of Abijah; and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
inside. And he kept making signs to them, and remained mute.
And when the days of his service were completed, he went to his
own house. And after those days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself for five months,
and she said: "Thus the Lord [?] me in these days, in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among people."
And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee whose name was Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house and tribe of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.
And the angel went in to her and said to her: "Rejoice, favored one!"
to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadows of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace."
And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day he was shown to Israel.
And in those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered.
This first registration took place when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
And everyone went to be registered, each to his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and tribe of David,
to be registered with Mary, who [?]
And all who heard were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept these words and pondered them in her heart.
And the shepherds turned back and went away, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told them.
And when the eight days were completed for his circumcision, they also called his name Jesus, the name he had been given by the angel before he was in his mother's womb.
And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought the child up to Jerusalem to present him
before the Lord, as it is written in the law of the Lord: "Every male that opens the womb [?] holy
...it shall be called [holy] to the Lord; and they were to offer a sacrifice, as it is said...
...was with the travelling company, and they went a day's journey, and they looked for him among their kinsfolk
and acquaintances, and they did not find him, and they turned back as far as Jerusalem, looking for him.
And it came to pass after three days that they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers and asking them questions.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and at his answers.
And they saw him and were astonished, and his mother said to him: "Son, why have you done this to us? Behold, your father and I have been searching for you in distress [?], and
seeking you." And he said to them: "Why were you seeking me? Did you not know that in my Father's house it is fitting
for me to be?" And they did not understand the word that he spoke to them.
And he went with them.
And Jesus too was baptized, and as he was praying,
the heavens were opened, and the Holy Spirit came down upon him in bodily form, like a dove, and a voice came from heaven and said: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
And Jesus himself was beginning to be about his thirtieth year, being, as was supposed, the son of Joseph,
of Jacob, [?] of Matthan, [?] of Jannai, of Joseph,
of Mattathias, of Amos, of Nahum, of Esli,
of Naggai, of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, [?] of Judah,
of Joanan, of Rhesa, [?] of Shealtiel,
of Neri, of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
of Joshua, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonam,
of Eliakim, of Melea, of Menna, of Nathan, of David,
of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Salmon, of Nahshon,
of Amminadab, of Aram, of Hezron, of Perez,
of Judah, of Jacob, of Isaac, of Abraham, of Terah,
of Nahor, of Serug, of Reu, of Peleg, of Eber, of Shelah,
of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,
son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel,
son of Cainan, son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.
And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
and for forty days he was tempted by the devil. And he ate nothing in those days, and when those days were completed, he was hungry.
And the devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
And he laid his hand on each one of them and healed them.
And demons came out of many, crying out and saying, "You are the Christ, the Son of God." And he rebuked them and did not allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
And when day broke, he went out from there and went to a deserted place. And the crowd was looking for him, and they came to him and tried to hold him back so that he would not go away from them.
But he said to them, "I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities as well, for that is why I was sent."
And he was preaching in all the synagogues of Galilee.
And it happened, as the crowd was [?pressing upon] him to hear the word of God, and he was standing by the shore of the lake of Gennesaret,
that he saw two boats standing at the shore of the lake; but the fishermen had gone out of the boat and were washing
their nets. And he went in [?] and he told them to put out a little from the land. And he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
And when he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "[?] into the deep, and let down [?] for a catch."
Simon answered and said to him, "Master, we toiled all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will let down the net."
[?] they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were breaking.
of theirs. And they signalled to those who were in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell at the knees of Jesus and said to him, "Depart from me, for a sinful man
am I, O Lord." For amazement had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish that they had taken;
and likewise James and John, the sons of [?], who were Simon's partners. And Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid, Simon; from now on you will be a catcher of men."
And they brought the boat to land, left everything, and followed him.
And it happened, when he entered one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, begged him and said,
"Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored
like the other. But they were filled with wickedness and were discussing with one another what they might do to Jesus.
twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he called Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew
Matthew and
with them, and he stood in a level place, and the crowd of his disciples, and a very great multitude of other people from Judea and Jerusalem and from the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon
And all the crowd sought to come near him, for power went out from him and all were healed.
And he lifted up his eyes toward the disciples and said: Blessed are you poor
But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.
Woe to you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn.
Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you
and bless those who curse you, and pray for those who
And just as you wish people to do to you, you also likewise, in the same way
And if you love those who love you
And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive back, what grace is that to you? For sinners also lend to sinners, so that they may receive back the same amount.
And what fell among the thorns, these are those who hear the word, and as they go on their way they are choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of this world, and they bear no fruit.
But what fell on the good ground, these are those who hear the word with a good and kind heart, and keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed, but sets it on a lampstand so that those who come in may see the light.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not become known and come into the open.
So take heed how you hear: whoever has, to him more will be given, and whoever does not
And he got into the boat and returned back.
The man from whom the demons had been cast out begged him that he might be with him; but he sent him away and said to him:
Return to your house and tell how much God has done for you. And he went away and proclaimed throughout the whole [?] what Jesus had done for him.
And when Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were waiting for
him. And behold, a man came whose name was Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue; and he fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come into his house,
for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. And
He took the child's hand and called out: Child, arise.
And her spirit returned, and she rose at once, and he ordered that she be given something to eat.
And her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.
And he called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to heal diseases.
And he sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
And he said to them: Take nothing for the road: no bags, no bread, no silver, and do not
have two garments. And whatever house [?] you [enter], stay there and go out from there.
…that I am? And they answered and said to him: John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and some say that one of the earlier prophets
has risen. And Jesus said to them: But who do you think I am?
and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and to be killed, and on the third day to rise.
And he said to all those who wish to follow
him before him, and said: Whoever receives this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For whoever is least among all of you, he is great.
John answered and said to him: Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow us.
Jesus said to him: Do not stop him, for whoever is not against us is on our side.
And it came to pass, when the days of his being taken up were fulfilled, that he himself set his face
to go up to Jerusalem. And he sent messengers ahead of him, and they went and entered a village of the Samaritans to prepare something for
him. And they did not receive them, because his face was set toward going
to Jerusalem. When they saw
And he bandaged his wounds, pouring oil and wine on them, and put him on his own animal, and brought him to the inn and took care of him.
And the next day, as he was leaving, he gave two denarii to the innkeeper and said to him: Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.
Which of these three do you think was a neighbour to the man who fell
among robbers? And he said: The one who showed him mercy. Jesus said to him: Go and do the same.
And as they went on, he entered a certain village, where there was a woman named Martha, and she welcomed him into her house.
And she had a sister called Mary, who sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his words.
But Martha was distracted by much serving. She came up and said: Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me.
Jesus answered and said to her: Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled
about many things. Here little is needed. But Mary has chosen the good portion, which will never be taken away from her.
And he was in a place where he himself was praying, and when he stopped praying, one of his disciples said to him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples."
And he said to them, "When you pray, say: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done."
"Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened
to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened."
"Which of you who is a father, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish,
will he give him a scorpion?
If, then, you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father give the Holy Spirit from heaven to those who ask him!"
And he cast a demon that was mute out of a certain man. And when the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and all the people were amazed.
But some of them said, "He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons."
And others, testing him, asked him for a sign from heaven.
But he knew their thoughts and said to them, "Every kingdom that is divided against itself is laid waste, and house upon house
[?] ... If the devil
by Beelzebul cast out demons, by what do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves will become your judges.
But if I cast out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man, armed,
did not first wash before the meal.
The Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Fools! Did not the one who made the outside also
make the inside? But give as alms what is proper, and behold, everything is clean for you.
But woe to you Pharisees! For you take a tithe of mint and rue and every herb, and you pass over justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone.
Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the chief seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you! For you are
some of them they will kill
and persecute, so that the blood of all the prophets, shed since the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, who perished between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation."
Woe to you, teachers of the law, for you have hidden the keys of knowledge [?]
[?] the scribes and the Pharisees began to plot evil, and the word was grievous to them, and [?]
[?] from his mouth, so that they might accuse him.

Meanwhile, when a great multitude of people had gathered, so that they were even trampling one another, he began first to say to his disciples: "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
But there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
Therefore whatever you say in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you speak into the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
But I say to you, my friends: do not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have nothing more that they can do to you.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear him who [?]
for they neither sow nor reap; they have no storehouse or barn where they can gather, and God feeds them. How much better you are than the birds!
Which of you by worrying can add to his stature
one cubit? If then you are not able to do even the least thing, why do you worry about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin; but I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If then God so clothes the grass in the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith!
And you, do not seek what you will eat and what [?], and do not
be anxious; for all the nations of the world seek all these things, and your Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give them away; give alms. Make for yourselves wealth that does not grow old, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
[?] treasure [?] there will your heart be also.
Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.
And be like men who are waiting for their lord
his own, and did not [?] his, will be punished severely.

But the one who did not know, and did something deserving punishment, will suffer little. For from everyone to whom much was given, much will be required, and from the one to whom much was entrusted, even more will be demanded.
I came to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I wish [?] if it were already kindled!
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am constrained until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I have come to spread peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
For from now on there will be five in one house, divided, three against two and two against three.
They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her son's wife and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.
He also said to the people: When you see a cloud rising from the west, you say at once, "Rain is coming," and so it happens [?]
And when the wind blows from the south, you say, "There will be heat," and so it happens.
So, hypocrites, you know how to test the face of the earth and of the sky, but how is it that you do not test this time?
Or why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you are going with your adversary before the ruler, make an effort on the way to be released from him, so that he does not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer put you in prison.
I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid even the last mite.
At that very time some people came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus answered and said to them: Do you think that these Galileans were greater sinners than all the Galileans, because they suffered such things?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they alone were more guilty than all the people who live in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish likewise.
And he told them this parable: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it, and

found none. And he said to the vinedresser: Look, for three years now I have been coming and looking for fruit on this fig tree, and I have found none. Cut it down. Why should it even take up the ground for nothing?
But he answered and said to him: Lord, leave it this year too, until I dig around it and put
down manure. And if it bears fruit, [well]; but if not, then cut it down.
And he was teaching them in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not stand up straight at all.
Jesus saw her, called her over, and said to her: Woman, you are set free from your
infirmity. And he laid his hands on her, and at once she stood up straight, walked, and glorified God.

The ruler of the synagogue answered angrily, because he had healed on the Sabbath, and said to the people: There are six days on which it is right to work. Come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.
The Lord answered him and said: Hypocrites, does not each one of you untie his ox or donkey from his manger, lead it away, and give
it water? And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom the devil bound, behold, for eighteen years now: was it not right for her to be loosed from her bonds on the Sabbath day?
And when he said this, all his adversaries were put to shame [?], and all the people rejoiced over all the glorious things that were done by him.
And the Lord said: What is the kingdom of God like, and to what is it to be compared?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky made their dwelling in its branches.
Then he said again: To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed in [?]
... for me to go on tomorrow and the day after, for it is not fitting for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who killed the prophets and stoned those who were sent [to you]!
Your houses are left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me from now on until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'
And it happened, as he was going . . . [?]
and he will say to you, 'Give this man your place,' and then with shame you will begin to take the lowest place.

But when someone invites you, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will have honour before all who are reclining at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

He also said to the one who had invited him: When you give a dinner or a supper, do not invite your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor your rich neighbours, lest they also invite you in return and it become a repayment to you.
But when you give a dinner, invite the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind.
And you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you, and you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
One of those reclining at table with him heard this and said to him: Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of God.
But he said to him: A certain man gave a great banquet and invited many.
And at the hour of the banquet he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited to come, for behold, everything is ready.
And they all, one by one, began to make excuses. The first said to him: I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. I beg you, excuse me; let me be excused by you.
And another said:
Clothe him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes
on his feet, and bring the fatted calf and kill it, and let us eat
and rejoice, for this son of mine was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found. And they began to make merry.
Now his elder son was out in the field, and as he was coming up and drew near the house, he heard the sound of rejoicing and merrymaking.
And he called one of the servants and asked him what [?]
"What is this?" And he said to him, "Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back alive."
But he became angry and would not go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

And he answered and said to his father, "Look, all these years I have served you, and I have never disobeyed your command, yet you have never given me even one young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, who has eaten up your property with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him."
And he said to him, "Child, you are always with me, and everything that is mine
is yours. It was right to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found."
And he said to the disciples: "There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and it was reported to him that the steward was wasting his goods.
And he called him and said to him, 'What is this that . . . [?]'
"No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
The Pharisees also heard all this, because they were lovers of money, and they scorned him.
And he said to them, "You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts. For what is exalted among people is detestable before God.
The law and the prophets were until John. Since then the good news of the kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone forces his way into it.
It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and whoever marries a woman divorced by her husband also commits adultery.
There was a certain rich man who was dressed in purple and fine linen and who feasted splendidly every day.
There was a poor man named Lazarus. He lay at his gates and [?].
And he longed to be filled with the crumbs that fell from that rich man's table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
The poor man died, and he was carried by angels to Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
[?] . . . were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these
little ones to stumble. But be on your guard. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
And even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and turns back to you seven times and says to you, 'I repent,' forgive him."
The apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith."
The Lord said to them, "If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you could say to this sycamore tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Which of you who has a servant plowing or tending sheep would say to him at once, when he comes in from the field, 'Come here and sit down'?
For the kingdom of God is like this.
Amen, I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.
And a certain ruler asked him, saying, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except only
God. You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honour your father and your mother
your [...]." But he said, "All these I have kept since my youth."
When Jesus heard this, he said to him, "You still lack this one thing: sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."
When he heard this, he became sorrowful, for he was
very rich. When Jesus saw him, he said, "How hard [?] the kingdom of God for those who have wealth.
It is easier for a ship's cable to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to [enter] the kingdom of God"
to enter." Those who heard this said, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus answered and said, "What is impossible for people is possible for God."
Peter said to him, "Look, we have left everything of our own and followed you."
He said to them, "Amen, I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom
of God who will not receive many times as much in this time
because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
And he ran ahead [?] and climbed a sycamore tree to see him, for he was about to pass
that way. And when he came to that place, Jesus looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house."
And he hurried and came down and welcomed him with joy.
And when they saw [?], they grumbled and said, "He has gone in to stay with a sinful man."
Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, half of my goods [?] I give, and if I have falsely accused anyone of anything, I give back four times as much."
And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, for this man too is a son of Abraham.

For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." And as the crowd listened, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear at once.
And he said to them, "A certain nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and then return.
And he called ten of his servants, gave them ten minas, and said to them, 'Trade with this until I come.'
But his citizens hated him and sent a messenger after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
And it came to pass at his return, when he had received his kingdom, that he commanded those servants to whom he had given the silver to be called, so that he might know what
[?] the whole multitude of the disciples [began] with joy to praise God with a loud voice for all those
mighty works which they had seen, and they said: Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.
And certain Pharisees [?] your disciples, that they may be silent.
But Jesus answered and said to them: I tell you that if these are silent, the stones will cry out.
And when he drew near, he saw the city and wept over it,
and said: If only you had known on this day what is for your peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when your enemies will bring an army against you and surround you and hem you in on every side,

and they will tear you down, and your children within you will be dashed to the ground, and not one stone will be left upon another within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.
And when he entered the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling doves,
and he said to them: It is written: My house shall be a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers.
And he was teaching daily in the temple; but the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people sought to destroy him,
and they could find nothing they might do, for all the people were devoted to hearing him.
And it came to pass in those days, when [?] he was teaching
And Jesus said to them: Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this.
And he began to speak to them in a parable: A certain man planted a vineyard and let it out to tenants and went away for a long time.
And at the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, so that they would give him some of its fruit; but the tenants beat him and tormented him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he sent yet another servant; but they beat him too and sent him away empty-handed.
Then he sent a third once more; but they seized him and wounded him and threw him out.
And the lord of the vineyard said: What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps [?] they will respect this one.

Teacher, you have spoken well.

And while all the people were listening, he said to his disciples:
"Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes, and who love to be greeted in the streets, and to have the first seats in the synagogue and the places of honour at feasts;
who devour the houses of widows and, as a pretence, pray at length. These will receive the greater condemnation."
He looked up and saw those who were putting offerings into the treasury,
the rich. And he saw a certain poor widow, who put in
two mites. And Jesus said, "Truly I tell you that this poor widow has offered more than all of them.
For all these offered out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, offered everything she had."
And some were saying of the temple that it was built with fine and precious stones, and he said:
"Do you see this? The days will come in which not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down."
The disciples asked, "Teacher, when will this be, and what will be the sign when this is about to happen?"
And he said, "See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name and say, 'I am he,' and 'The time has drawn near.' [?] to follow them.
When you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified, for this must happen, but the end will not come at once."
Then he said to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against
kingdom. There will be great earthquakes, and famines in various places, and [?] terrors from heaven, and there will be great signs.
But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, and hand you over to synagogues and prisons; they will bring you before kings and governors for the sake of my
name. And this will be a testimony for you.
So settle this in your hearts: you are not to prepare in advance any word
of reply. For I will give you a mouth and wisdom which none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or answer.
For you will be handed over by fathers and mothers, and brothers, and friends, and kinsmen, and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by all for the sake of my name.
And not a hair of your head will
perish. By your endurance you will gain your souls.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its desolation has drawn near.
